newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Leong takes controlling stake in HK Marriott.
newsitem.headline: Hong Leong takes controlling stake in HK Marriott.

text.p: Singapore's Hong Leong Group has acquired a controlling stake in the Marriott Hotel Hong Kong, said a statement issued on Monday by Hong Leong's listed hotel arm, CDL Hotels International Ltd.
The statement quoted Hong Leong Group executive chairman Kwek Leng Beng as saying the deal allowed the Singapore group to own a second hotel in Hong Kong. CDL Hotels also owns Hotel Nikko Hong Kong.
Swire Properties Ltd said earlier on Monday it had agreed to sell its 80 percent stake in Queensway Hotel Ltd, which owns the JW Marriott Hotel in Hong Kong, for an undisclosed figure.
The buyer is Chishore Enterprise Inc, 65 percent owned by Hotel Nikko Hong Kong Ltd and 35 percent by Recosia Pte Ltd. Hotel Nikko is 95.45 percent owned by Asean Resources Holdings Ltd and CDL.
Recosia is wholly owned by the Singapore government.
"It is a good deal. We look forward to working with Swire and Marriott which has been successfully managing the hotel," Kwek, who is also chairman of CDL Hotels, was quoted as saying.

"Swire Properties intends to retain its 20 percent interest in Queensway as a long-term investment in line with its 20 percent interest in each of the companies owning the Conrad International and Island Shangri-La Hotels in Pacific Place," Swire Properties managing director Keith Kerr said in a statement.
